predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: Masovia proper and eastern Kuyavia, the share of Bolesław IV the Curly under the 1138 testament

successors.name: Kingdom of Poland
successors.text: Masovia as Cliopatria draws it in its last year; the Kingdom of Poland shape of 1352 covers 131 of its 132 cells

ledger.x: 1138: Bolesław III's testament creates the Duchy of Masovia for Bolesław IV the Curly.
1146: Bolesław IV the Curly becomes High Duke and takes the Seniorate and Silesia.
1163: Silesia returns to Władysław II's sons.
January 1173: Bolesław IV dies and Mieszko III takes the Seniorate.
1186: Leszek of Masovia dies; Casimir II takes Masovia proper and Mieszko III Kuyavia.
1186: Mieszko III of Greater Poland occupies Kuyavia 'up to the Vistula River' on Leszek's death.
1199: Konrad I receives Masovia.
1205: Konrad I adds Kuyavia.
1229: Konrad I takes the title of High Duke.
1230: Konrad cedes the Chełmno Land to the Teutonic Order.
1232: Henry I the Bearded of Silesia becomes High Duke at Kraków.
1233: Konrad gives Kuyavia to his son.
1235: Konrad of Masovia takes the Radom district.
9 July 1239: Konrad gives up on Sandomierz at Przedbórz.
10 July 1241: Konrad I enters Kraków.
25 May 1243: Bolesław V wins Kraków at Suchodoły.
1248: Casimir I of Kuyavia takes the Dobrzyń Land from his brother's heirs.
1262: the dukes' seat moves from Płock to Czersk.
1326: a strip on the north-eastern edge goes to Lithuania.
1351: the Masovian dukes become vassals of the Polish king.

wars.name: Polish campaign of Frederick Barbarossa (1157)
wars.outcome: Bolesław IV was 'declared a vassal of the Empire at his camp in Krzyszkowo' on 30 August 1157, begged forgiveness on his knees and 'had to pay an enormous tribute'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Bolesław IV's Prussian campaign
wars.outcome: 'efforts and attempts to conquer these provinces were finally defeated in 1166'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Konrad I's wars with the Old Prussians
wars.outcome: 'Several further campaigns in 1219, 1222 failed'; in 1226 Konrad called the Teutonic Order and in 1230 ceded the Chełmno Land to the knights.

wars.name: Konrad I's bid for the High Duchy (1229-1232)
wars.outcome: Konrad took the title of High Duke in 1229 against Spindleshanks and held it to 1232, when Henry I the Bearded prevailed at Kraków.

wars.name: Konrad I's invasion of Sandomierz (1235-1239)
wars.outcome: After the Treaty of Luchani Konrad invaded Sandomierz and Bolesław V lost the Radom district (1235); at Przedbórz on 9 July 1239 Konrad renounced his claims over Sandomierz.

wars.name: Konrad I's second bid for Kraków (1241-1243)
wars.outcome: Konrad entered Kraków on 10 July 1241 (Bolesław V page; infobox High Duke 1241-1243) and Bolesław V regained it at Suchodoły on 25 May 1243.

wars.name: First Mongol invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: Sandomierz sacked on 13 February 1241, Kraków seized by 24 March, Legnica on 9 April; the Mongols left and 'Ögedei's death probably saved the Polish lands from being completely overrun'.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: 'Duke Wenceslaus of Płock' was an ally of the Order; the Order 'pillaged and conquered the Polish Kuyavian region and the Dobrzyń Land'; the Treaty of Kalisz (1343) returned the Dobrzyń Land to Poland.

wars.name: Lithuanian-Masovian conflict of 1326
wars.outcome: A short conflict between Poland's ally Lithuania and the Masovian dukes after the 1326 Brodnica agreement between Trojden I and the Teutonic Order.

certainty.note: A duchy of castellany districts with Prussian, Yotvingian and Rus' marches: no page opened gives a surveyed or treaty boundary.
